extracted.intended_audience: researchers, prospective students, industry partners, funders, and the general public interested in TUM's research strategy
extracted.subtask_description: Institutional statement of research goals and quality expectations at the Technical University of Munich (TUM), emphasising society-centered innovation, interdisciplinarity, infrastructure, training, and translational impact. Useful for aligning research proposals, institutional strategies, or describing evaluative priorities for grants and collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Society-centered research and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: “Society-centered research and innovation” is the goal we have set ourselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue a holistic approach that puts people at the center; research and innovations should be needed and accepted by society. Examples and coverage on the page stress making innovations trustworthy and socially acceptable (see interview).

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic assessment of consequences and risks
rubrics_metrics.description: We therefore pursue a holistic approach and take into account economic, ecological, social, political and ethical/moral consequences and risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research planning and innovation should explicitly consider multiple consequence domains (economic, ecological, social, political, ethical). This is presented as an operational imperative rather than optional reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trustworthiness and social acceptance of innovations
rubrics_metrics.description: We want to launch trustworthy innovations that are accepted and needed in society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovations should be evaluated for trustworthiness and likelihood of societal acceptance; see interview 'Making innovations trustworthy and socially acceptable' for further emphasis. Implicit anti-pattern: technically novel but socially rejected technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary research
rubrics_metrics.description: In research and innovation, we work at the interface between technology, economics, politics, society and ecology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage work across disciplinary boundaries and interfaces; organisational structures (Schools linked by integrative research institutes and Clusters of Excellence) are used to enable interdisciplinarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational agility and creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: To this end, our scientists conduct interdisciplinary, operationally agile and creative research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research groups are expected to be operationally agile (able to adapt quickly) and creative in approach. This is presented as a desired mode of working rather than a metric with numeric scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing fundamental and major societal challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploring the origins of the universe and the foundations of life, seeking solutions to the major challenges of our time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TUM positions research to cover both fundamental science (origins, foundations) and applied work that addresses pressing societal problems (climate, health, energy). Proposals should align with either deep fundamentals or societally relevant problem-solving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability, cost-effectiveness and practicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Our task as a technical university is to find sustainable, cost-effective and practicable solutions for the future energy supply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When developing technologies (energy, agriculture, mobility), prioritise sustainability, affordability, and practical deployability. Explicit example: energy research should balance sustainability with cost and practicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety, affordability and sustainability in mobility
rubrics_metrics.description: We are researching future-proof solutions in the field of urban mobility to make transportation safe, affordable and sustainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mobility research should target multi-dimensional outcomes (safety, affordability, sustainability); proposed solutions that only address one dimension are implicitly incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellent research infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality facilities and infrastructure are a core expectation to support excellent research (the page emphasises infrastructure as foundational). This supports claims about capacity to execute ambitious projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clusters of Excellence and collaborative partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: The seven Clusters of Excellence ... together with national and international partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research excellence is pursued via organised cluster structures and partnerships; collaborative, cross-institutional projects and participation in clusters are highlighted as pathways to excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and development of highly qualified talent
rubrics_metrics.description: We also train highly qualified young talent. Careers in research: Be part of the research community as a PhD student, postdoc or professor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful research programme should include education and training components (PhD, postdoc mentoring) that develop future researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support services for researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: We offer comprehensive support for researchers – for funding, continuing education and start-up consulting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional support (funding advice, continuing education, start-up consulting) is part of the research ecosystem and an expectation for enabling research impact and translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose-driven innovation for people and nature
rubrics_metrics.description: We develop innovative technologies not for the sake of it, but for people and nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research and technology development should be justified by positive human and environmental outcomes rather than novelty alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement and outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Engagement – bringing science and society closer together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active engagement with the public (communication, outreach, magazine, events) is an explicit institutional goal; scholars should incorporate dissemination and engagement activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of teaching and research across schools and institutes
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation of our university is formed by seven Schools, which are linked at the interface of disciplines by integrative research institutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural integration is emphasised: link research to teaching and organise across institutional boundaries to foster integrative research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational and applied impact examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of applied outcomes: early warning system for forest fires; exoskeleton/electrical stimulation for stroke rehabilitation; imaging tech to reduce culling of male chicks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page foregrounds translational research that produces concrete applications and societal benefit; successful projects are those that move from research to tested applications or startups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to highest quality standards (University of Excellence)
rubrics_metrics.description: TUM has been one of Germany's Universities of Excellence since 2006 – we remain committed to this highest of quality standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional recognition and sustained commitment to formal excellence benchmarks are emphasised as evidence of quality; aligning with these standards supports reputation and funding competitiveness.
